title: Proofreaders and Copy Markers
description: Read transcript or proof type setup to detect and mark for correction any grammatical, typographical, or compositional errors. Excludes workers whose primary duty is editing copy. Includes proofreaders of braille.

clusters.label: Evaluating Information to Determine Compliance with Standards

tasks.text: Mark copy to indicate and correct errors in type, arrangement, grammar, punctuation, or spelling, using standard printers' marks.
Read corrected copies or proofs to ensure that all corrections have been made.
Correct or record omissions, errors, or inconsistencies found.
Typeset and measure dimensions, spacing, and positioning of page elements, such as copy and illustrations, to verify conformance to specifications, using printer's ruler or layout software.
Read proof sheets aloud, calling out punctuation marks and spelling unusual words and proper names.
Consult reference books or secure aid of readers to check references with rules of grammar and composition.
Archive documents, conduct research, and read copy, using the internet and various computer programs.
Compare information or figures on one record against same data on other records, or with original copy, to detect errors.
Route proofs with marked corrections to authors, editors, typists, or typesetters for correction or reprinting.

clusters.label: Communicating with Supervisors, Peers, or Subordinates

tasks.text: Consult with authors and editors regarding manuscript changes and suggestions.

clusters.label: Communicating with People Outside the Organization

tasks.text: Write original content, such as headlines, cutlines, captions, and cover copy.

skills.name: Reading Comprehension
skills.def: Understanding written sentences and paragraphs in work-related documents.

skills.name: Writing
skills.def: Communicating effectively in writing as appropriate for the needs of the audience.

skills.name: Speaking
skills.def: Talking to others to convey information effectively.

skills.name: Active Listening
skills.def: Giving full attention to what other people are saying, taking time to understand the points being made, asking questions as appropriate, and not interrupting at inappropriate times.

skills.name: Critical Thinking
skills.def: Using logic and reasoning to identify the strengths and weaknesses of alternative solutions, conclusions, or approaches to problems.

skills.name: Monitoring
skills.def: Monitoring/Assessing performance of yourself, other individuals, or organizations to make improvements or take corrective action.

skills.name: Time Management
skills.def: Managing one's own time and the time of others.

skills.name: Graphics or photo imaging software
skills.def: Software to draw or manipulate images. May adjust colors, add text, or apply special effects. Examples: Adobe Creative Cloud software, Adobe Illustrator, Adobe Photoshop.

skills.name: Word processing software
skills.def: Software to create, edit, store, or print documents. Examples: Adobe InCopy, After the Deadline, AutoCrit Editing Wizard, Elite Minds RightWriter.

skills.name: Desktop publishing software
skills.def: Software to create or edit text and graphics into documents such as books, magazines, brochures, or manuals. Examples: Adobe FrameMaker, Adobe InDesign, QuarkXPress.

skills.name: Presentation software
skills.def: Software to create presentations, speeches, or slideshows. Examples: Apple iWork Keynote, Microsoft PowerPoint.

skills.name: Spreadsheet software
skills.def: Software to create or edit numbers or text organized into rows and columns of cells. May include formulas which recalculate values based on other cells. Examples: Microsoft Excel.

skills.name: Office suite software
skills.def: Software to provide word processing, spreadsheet, e-mail, presentations, or data management capabilities. Examples: Microsoft Office software.
